name: Electrical Materials Co
old_description: Since 1961 Electrical Materials Company has been a manufacturer, developer, and supplier of products to serve the needs of The Electrical Utility, Telephone and CATV industries. Our multifaceted manufacturing capacity allows us to meet the needs of our diverse customer base. Some of our products include Cable Enclosures, Guy Markers, U-Guards™ (pole risers), Wildlife Protectors, Transformer Accessories, Secondary Service Pedestals, RV Electrical Service Pedestals, Posts, and Cable Markers.
about:
Electrical Materials Company has operated from Earlville, Illinois since its founding in 1961. The business also maintains a facility in Genoa City, Wisconsin. No founders are named in public records, and ownership structure is not disclosed.

The company manufactures a range of pole‑line and underground distribution hardware for electric utilities, telephone and CATV providers. Its product line includes cable enclosures, guy markers, U‑Guard™ pole risers (both steel and plastic), wildlife protectors, transformer accessories, secondary service pedestals (steel rounded, rectangular or square), RV and mobile‑home power pedestals (metered and unmetered), mounting posts, brackets, ground‑wire molding, conduit duct plugs and cable markers. The firm pioneered the flanged U‑Guard design in the early 1960s and introduced the first secondary service pedestals to the market in 1961.

Primary customers are investor‑owned and municipal electric utilities, telephone companies, cable‑TV operators, and RV‑park developers. The company also supplies contractors who install overhead and underground distribution systems. Examples from its catalog include transformer mounting cleats for utility substations, perch guards for avian protection, and ergonomic lineman tools such as blanket clamp hooks and outrigger pads.

Electrical Materials Company emphasizes its early‑mover advantage in pole‑riser and pedestal design, stating it remains a leader in quality and innovation for electrical pedestals, cabinets and enclosures. UL‑listed products and a focus on lineman safety through ergonomic tool design are cited as ongoing differentiators.
